pairs.subject: remote-capability-probing
pairs.evidence: crates/core/src/resilience/mod.rs:13 The module judges extraction and fetch health (bot walls, 5xx, selector rebinds) from stored history, which is the health-checks neighbour's present-tense question rather than a per-peer how-to-address-it verdict; searching crates/core and the context's tests for accept-ranges, partial_content, content-range, bytes=0- and readahead found zero hits, so no fragment-read probe, capability ladder or read buffer exists here.

techniques.evidence: crates/core/src/resilience/detect.rs:182 FetchHealth classifies response statuses for retirement and health judgement; it never accepts a capability from a peer's header or a provoked response.

crates/core/src/doctor.rs:124 The doctor's three-valued outcome looks like basis tagging, but it reports on the local SQLite store and artifact tree. It is not a feature report about a hosted platform.

pairs.subject: remote-capability-probing
pairs.evidence: crates/server/src/routes/remote.rs:1 The only remote-facing file in this context is the serving side of the fetch fabric. It is the peer that gets asked, not the prober: it runs a coordinator's whole-request fetch through the local engine and never works out what an upstream peer can do. Searching crates/server/src/routes for accept-ranges, partial_content, content-range and bytes=0- found zero hits.

techniques.evidence: crates/server/src/routes/remote.rs:197 The route proxies one whole request and returns the envelope as it is. No branch reads a peer's capability advertisement.

crates/server/src/routes/remote.rs:184 The body cap is a node ceiling on every proxied fetch. It is not a refusal ceiling on a fallback that swaps a fragment read for a whole-object read, because there are no fragment reads.
crates/server/src/routes/remote.rs:152 These guards are the serving node's own admission checks. They are not a prober's preflight in front of capability rows.

pairs.subject: remote-capability-probing
pairs.evidence: crates/core/src/cache.rs:128 The cache stores whole responses and uses only ETag/Last-Modified conditional revalidation, which belongs to client-fetch-cache. It never decides whether a peer can serve fragments. Searching crates/core for accept-ranges, partial_content, content-range, bytes=0- and readahead found zero hits, so there is no capability verdict, fallback rung or latency-class buffer to judge.

techniques.evidence: crates/core/src/cache.rs:151 Stored validators feed a conditional GET. That is cache revalidation, not a capability accepted from an advertisement.
crates/core/src/lru.rs:2 The LRU tracks a pool of client and browser handles. It is not a file-shaped buffer over backing stores at different distances.
crates/core/src/cache.rs:192 The revalidation log counts changed and unchanged results on whole-response revalidation. There is no readahead or fragment byte counter whose cause could be split out.
